title: review: R14c: orchestrator/jev_points.py — experimental Jev decision points (scout necessity, context escalation, review escalation, planner relaunch), shadow by default, escalate-only in active, fail-open (Phase I P7)
spec:
Why: Phase I P7 names four experimental Jev decision points introduced independently: scout necessity, context escalation, review escalation (never overriding the mandatory security review) and Planner relaunch. Today planner_runs.jev_triage (orchestrator/planner_runs.py:432-460) records one generic shadow choice for scouts_done/held/closable decision kinds and decision.py has no Jev use; nothing covers the four named points (audit T-0573).
What: new pure module orchestrator/jev_points.py using jev.ask (fail-open, returns None on any failure) and decision_log.record(kind="routing" is wrong here: use kind "scout" for scout necessity, "review_plan" for review escalation, "strategy" for context escalation and planner relaunch, with extra={"point": name}).
- POINTS = ("scout_necessity", "context_escalation", "review_escalation", "planner_relaunch"); each has its own mode under [jev.points] <point> = off|shadow|active (default shadow; unknown -> shadow) and a typed question set (noul probabilities) with a bounded, redacted state: task title, spec[:600] via jev.redact, acceptance count, scope list, complexity, task_class, memory titles, deterministic evidence supplied by the caller (e.g. scout_evidence.reuse_check result, packet size, review plan). Never file contents.
- ask(point, task, evidence, *, cfg=None, ask_fn=jev.ask) -> {"point", "mode", "signals", "confidence", "suggestion", "applied": bool, "error"}: suggestion per point: scout_necessity -> "launch"|"skip"; context_escalation -> "expand"|"keep"; review_escalation -> "add_review"|"keep"; planner_relaunch -> "relaunch"|"wait". off -> no call, suggestion None. shadow -> call and record, applied False. active -> applied True only for escalating suggestions (launch a scout that deterministic reuse says is unnecessary is NOT escalation and stays a suggestion; expand context, add a review, relaunch are escalations); de-escalations (skip scout, keep smaller context, fewer reviews) are never applied; review_escalation can never reduce reviews or replace the security review (documented and tested); any failure -> suggestion None, error set, applied False.
- Every call records a decision_log row with candidates (the two options), hard_constraints (["security_review_deterministic", "required_reviews_floor"] for review_escalation), deterministic evidence, jev signals, selected, reason, confidence, mode.
- summary(root=STATE) -> per point {n, agreement with deterministic evidence where comparable, mean_confidence} from decision rows, for later evaluation.
acceptance: tests/test_jev_points.py::test_default_shadow_records_suggestion_without_applying — empty config: scout_necessity calls ask once, returns suggestion skip with applied False and writes a decision row with extra.point
tests/test_jev_points.py::test_off_mode_makes_no_call — mode off for a point: ask_fn not called, suggestion None

tests/test_jev_points.py::test_active_applies_only_escalations — active review_escalation with add_review applies True; active scout_necessity with skip applies False; active context_escalation with keep applies False

tests/test_jev_points.py::test_review_escalation_never_reduces_or_replaces_security_review — a suggestion of fewer reviews is coerced to keep, hard_constraints list security_review_deterministic, and the deterministic review count in the returned evidence is unchanged
tests/test_jev_points.py::test_fail_open_and_privacy — ask_fn returning None yields error set, suggestion None, applied False; the state passed to ask_fn is redacted and contains no file contents

result.summary: Implementation matches the spec closely: POINTS/OPTIONS/KINDS align with decision_log's valid kinds, ask()/summary() signatures match jev.ask and decision_log.record/read_all, redaction of title/spec plus exclusion of content-ish evidence keys satisfies the privacy requirement (verified jev.redact strips TOKEN=... and long hex/base64 runs), and review_escalation structurally can never reduce or replace the security review since its OPTIONS only offer add_review/keep. All 5 named acceptance tests are present and pass (ran via unittest). One design gap noted below is worth a follow-up test but doesn't violate a stated acceptance criterion or the hard security constraint, so not blocking.

comments.issue: _scout_escalates defaults to True (treats a scout as necessary) whenever the caller's evidence contains none of scout_needed/needs_scout/necessary/reuse_check. Combined with _applied's `suggestion == "launch" and _scout_escalates(evidence)` (line 144), an active-mode scout_necessity point will auto-apply "launch" whenever evidence is simply absent, not only when evidence affirmatively supports launching. That silently overrides the orchestrator's stated default of zero scouts unless a named uncertainty justifies one. No acceptance test exercises applied=True for scout_necessity at all (test_active_applies_only_escalations only covers the skip case), so this path is unverified.
